title: Finite invariant norm pencils from affine orbit-separated pairs
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $Y$ be a proper $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $Y$ by $F$-automorphisms, without a faithfulness assumption. Let $M$ be any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $a,b\in\Gamma(Y,M)$. For $c\in\Gamma(Y,M)$ define $Y_c=\{y:c(y)\ne0\}$ and $Z(c)=Y\setminus Y_c$, using residue-field fibres [def-weil-residue-field]. Assume $U=Y_a$ and $V=Y_b$ are affine and $\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(a)$ is disjoint from $\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(b)$. Using pullback and sheaf tensor product [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $C=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*M$, $A=\bigotimes_g g^*a$ and $D=\bigotimes_g g^*b$, as sections of $C$. Then $C$ is invertible, $Z(A)=\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(a)$ and $Z(D)=\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(b)$. Both $a,b$ and $A,D$ generate their respective modules [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. The coordinate morphisms $f=[a:b]$ and $f_N=[A:D]$ to $\mathbf P^1_F$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For the standard coordinate opens $Q_0=D_+(T_0)$ and $Q_1=D_+(T_1)$ of $\mathbf P^1_F$, their inverse images as open subschemes are $f^{-1}Q_0=U$, $f^{-1}Q_1=V$, $f_N^{-1}Q_0=\bigcap_g g^{-1}U$ and $f_N^{-1}Q_1=\bigcap_g g^{-1}V$; all these opens are affine. For every $h\in G$ the canonical pullback-composition and factor-permutation isomorphism $h^*C\cong C$, reindexing $g$ by $gh$, carries $h^*A$ to $A$ and $h^*D$ to $D$, and $f_N\circ h=f_N$ as scheme morphisms. No ampleness, dimension, reducedness or smoothness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an ordering of the nonempty finite set $G$, and bracket all tensor products from the left. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], every $g^*M$ is invertible and induction on the number of factors makes $C$ invertible. For $c=a$ or $b$, put $N(c)=\bigotimes_g g^*c$. By [lem-sc-nonvanishing-tensor-pullback], $Y_{g^*c}=g^{-1}Y_c$. By [lem-sc-tensor-section-affine-open], $Y_{N(c)}=\bigcap_g g^{-1}Y_c$; taking complements gives $Z(N(c))=\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(c)$. The same tensor-section lemma proves these two intersections affine: the factor indexed by $1\in G$ has nonvanishing open $U$, respectively $V$, which is affine by hypothesis. Thus this also proves affineness without assuming an arbitrary intersection of affine opens is affine.

proof.text: The assumed disjointness and step 1 give $Z(A)\cap Z(D)=\varnothing$, so $Y_A\cup Y_D=Y$. Since the identity element is among the translates, $Z(a)\subseteq Z(A)$ and $Z(b)\subseteq Z(D)$, hence $Z(a)\cap Z(b)=\varnothing$ and $U\cup V=Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre] first to the invertible module $M$ and the pair $(a,b)$ and then to the invertible module $C$ and the pair $(A,D)$. Its nonzero residue-value criterion proves that both pairs generate. There is no reducedness assumption in that criterion.

Use [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] with base $\operatorname{Spec}F$, $n=1$, and each of the two generating pairs of step 2, obtaining the $F$-morphisms $f=[a:b]$ and $f_N=[A:D]$. By clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage], their chart preimages are, respectively, $U,V$ and $Y_A,Y_D$. Insert the equalities from step 1 to get the four asserted preimages. Equal underlying open sets define the same open subscheme (the structure sheaf is restricted to that open), so these are equalities of open subschemes as required.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space; relative construction after Definition 01NF

proof.text: Apply clauses (a) and (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}F$. They say that $Q_0,Q_1$ cover $\mathbf P^1_F$ and are affine. All four preimages in step 3 are affine, by the hypotheses for $U,V$ and step 1 for $Y_A,Y_D$. Therefore [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], applied to this two-open target cover separately for $f$ and $f_N$, shows that both morphisms are affine.

The structure morphism $q:\mathbf P^1_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with the finite coordinate index set $\{0,1\}$, hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Both maps of step 3 are over $F$, so their composites with $q$ are the given proper structure map of $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] to each commutative triangle to obtain properness of $f$ and $f_N$. Combining this with their affineness in step 4, the reverse implication of [lem-sfb-affine-proper-finite] proves that both maps are finite.

Write the left action as $(gh)(y)=g(h(y))$. For $h\in G$, the section-compatible tensor-pullback and composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2) identify $h^*C$ with $\bigotimes_{g\in G}(gh)^*M$. Use the factor-permutation isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal] to move the factor labelled $g$ to position $gh$. Right multiplication by $h$ is bijective, with inverse right multiplication by $h^{-1}$, so the result is an isomorphism $\lambda_h:h^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. For $c=a$ and for $c=b$, the section formulas in the same two cited statements send $h^*N(c)$ first to $\bigotimes_g(gh)^*c$ and then to $\bigotimes_k k^*c=N(c)$. Thus $\lambda_h(h^*A)=A$ and $\lambda_h(h^*D)=D$ as actual sections. Repeated automorphisms in a nonfaithful action remain separate indexed factors; the permutation argument never removes them.

source.place: Tags 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 01CA (section-tensor-product), pullback-composition and finite factor permutations

proof.text: By pullback compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points], the composite of $f_N\circ h$ with $\mathbf P^1_F\to\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ corresponds to the generating pair $(h^*C,h^*A,h^*D)$. Step 6 identifies that pair with $(C,A,D)$. The equivalent-pairs clause of the same statement therefore identifies this composite with that of $f_N$. The other components of these two maps, in $\operatorname{Spec}F$, agree because $h$ is an $F$-automorphism. The fibre-product uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] now proves $f_N\circ h=f_N$ as morphisms to $\mathbf P^1_F$. This establishes the asserted invariance on schemes, including nonreduced schemes.
